verdict.rationale: Gmail's documented REST API, authorized with OAuth 2.0, covers every verb in the story: reading mailbox data, triaging via labels and filters, creating drafts, and sending messages or drafts. Push notifications let an agent react to mailbox changes. However, the evidence shows no first-party connection built for Claude or ChatGPT, so any agent must be wired to the raw API. Community reports add friction: scopes are coarse, and apps needing read access must pass a costly security assessment. Missing for 10: an official agent connector or MCP server, machine-readable agent docs (llms.txt and the OpenAPI probes returned 404), fine-grained scopes for agents, and hands-on corroboration of end-to-end agent use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an external agent — Claude, ChatGPT, or my own — can read, triage, draft, and send my email end to end through a documented connection
